learning_outcomes.text: Students apply technical, legal, and normative principles to analyze energy efficiency potentials in various sectors such as industry, transport, and buildings, and develop specific efficiency strategies for different applications.
They design management systems and plan energy audits, carry out data collection, and evaluate the results.
Students design corresponding networked systems and utilize intelligent control and forecasting systems.
They consider approaches and trends in energy system transformation.
Students compare various communication technologies in the energy context and select suitable standards.

syllabus_topics: Fundamentals and Framework Conditions (e.g., energy flows, carriers, conversion; legal and normative bases; management systems and audits; economics and sustainability)
Areas of Application (e.g., industry and plants; data centers; transport and logistics; buildings)
Management and Analysis (e.g., PDCA, CIP, Change Management; data collection and statistical analysis; reporting and visualization)
Digitalization and Data Use (e.g., IoT and networked systems, Big Data and Data Mining, simulations and Digital Twins)
Intelligent Control and Forecasting (e.g., Model Predictive Control, AI-based control systems, forecasting models)
Energy System Transformation (e.g., electrification, sector coupling, self-consumption, grid services)
Career Perspectives (e.g., energy consulting, efficiency management)

assessment_methods.method: Combined exam (study project work and oral exam)

assessment_rules: Credit points are awarded upon successful completion of the module examination and proof of performance. The grade's importance for the final grade is in accordance with the study and examination regulations (SPO).
